title: Investigate hash-table saturation causing eviction thrash and KV-cache latency spikes
creator: Ava Chen
description: During a customer load test on 2025-02-08 we observed sustained KV cache latency spikes and a 20% increase in serving memory. Initial symptoms resembled eviction storms and slow requests under high-concurrency tails. Root cause triage indicates hash-table bucket saturation (uneven key distribution + high concurrency) leading to long chains and lock contention, which in turn caused eviction workers to thrash and temporarily delay reclaiming slabs. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations rolled out, and long-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
actions: Add fine-grained per-shard hash metrics (bucket depth distribution, longest chain, avg probes) to Grafana and alert on >95th percentile chain length
Implement adaptive eviction backpressure: if eviction latency > 200ms, throttle new insertions for best-effort workloads and route critical requests to fallback cache tier
Prototype per-shard rehash-on-demand to reduce worst-case bucket lengths; evaluate CPU and pause overhead in canary
Introduce lock-free read path for common-case single-entry lookup to reduce contention under heavy read concurrency
Improve KV key hashing by introducing an optional secondary mixing step for user-provided skewed namespace keys
Run large-scale synthetic workload to reproduce saturation scenarios and validate mitigations before rollout
Post-deploy runbook: steps to observe, mitigate, and rollback if rehash causes regressions
